correctness.rationale: Fixed m≥3, n→∞, hub-started genuine nonbacktracking excludes the incoming hub neighbor. Exact avoidance for s marked vertices in a petal is 1−hS=(m−s)/(m(s+1)) and 1−hN=(m−s)(m−s−1)/(m(m−1)(s+1)), confirmed independently for m=3..7. For a tagged finite set, conditional exclusion of the incoming vertex affects hazard by O(n^-2), because its preceding petal is marked with conditional probability O(n^-1); a fixed-k factorial-moment Poisson limit follows as multi-vertex same-petal hazards satisfy h(s)>h(1). Per-excursion mean length m+1 with geometric tail, maximal deviation O_p(sqrt(n log n))=o_p(n), transferring the Gumbel limit and its mean. The uniform one-site hazard gives a summable tail. Constants qS=(m+1)/(2m), qN=(m+2)/(2m), mean speedup (m+1)/(m+2). Finite checks alone do not prove the limit.

value.rationale: Windmill clique graph is a natural stress test for full coverage with a hub bottleneck: the two walks have equal mean excursion length but different probabilities of discovering the last rare vertices. A sharp Gumbel law with exact speedup across all fixed m≥3, requiring nontrivial dependent-excursion control, is mathematically useful, not just coupon-collector substitution.
